skill.name: when-reviewing-pull-request-orchestrate-comprehensive-code-revie
skill.description: Orchestrates a multi-agent pull request review workflow covering automated checks, specialist reviews, integration analysis, and final merge recommendations.
skill.summary: Coordinate structured pull request reviews across quality, security, performance, architecture, testing, and documentation checks.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and illustrative Bash examples rather than hidden executable code. No prompt injection or secret exfiltration intent was found. The main security concern is semantic: the workflow includes GitHub commands that can approve, label, comment on, and merge pull requests, including an admin merge example.

remediation.issue: GitHub PR mutation commands can change remote repository state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit maintainer confirmation before any gh command that approves, labels, comments on, requests changes, or merges a pull request.

remediation.issue: The security patch example uses an admin merge command.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the admin merge example or mark it as manual-only with repository owner approval and documented emergency criteria.

remediation.issue: Example shell scripts use variables in commands and temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate PR_NUMBER and REPO inputs, quote shell variables consistently, and use safe temporary files created with mktemp.

static_findings.snippet: - **`pr-manager`** - PR coordination, review orchestration, findings aggregation, author notificatio
- **`code-analyzer`** - Linting, static analysis, code complexity metrics
- **`code-analyzer`** - Code quality, readability, maintainability, DRY, SOLID principles
- **`security-manager`** - Security vulnerabilities, OWASP compliance, secrets scanning, auth/auth
- **`performance-analyzer`** - Performance regressions, algorithmic efficiency, resource optimizatio
- **`system-architect`** - Architectural consistency, design patterns, scalability, integration fit
- **`api-documentation-specialist`** - Code documentation, API docs, comments, examples
- **`dependency-analyzer`** - Dependency audit, outdated packages, security vulnerabilities
- **`test-coverage-reviewer`** - Coverage metrics, uncovered code paths, edge case testing
- **`system-integrator`** - Integration impact, breaking changes, backward compatibility
- **`devops-engineer`** - Deployment impact, infrastructure changes, rollback planning

content.value_statement: Large pull requests are hard to review consistently across quality, security, testing, and deployment concerns. This skill provides a structured multi-agent review workflow with clear gates, findings, and merge recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Defines a four-phase pull request review process from automated checks to final decision.
Coordinates specialist reviewer roles for code quality, security, performance, architecture, tests, and documentation.
Provides sample commands for claude-flow, test runners, coverage tools, build checks, and GitHub PR actions.
Specifies memory key patterns for storing review metadata, phase findings, and final summaries.
Includes decision rules for approve, request changes, and reject outcomes.
Includes a GraphViz process diagram for the review workflow.
limitations: It does not execute a review by itself; it requires compatible agents and local tooling.
Command examples need adaptation for each repository, language stack, and CI environment.
GitHub actions require repository permissions and should be confirmed before changing remote state.
The four-hour timeline and quality metrics are workflow targets, not guaranteed results.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Reviews
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable review process for pull requests that need consistent quality gates and clear merge decisions.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Security Review
use_cases.description: Add focused security checks to a broader pull request review without losing context from quality and deployment findings.

use_cases.title: Improve Developer Platform Workflows
use_cases.description: Document a multi-agent review process that combines automation, specialist feedback, memory storage, and GitHub status updates.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with read-only checks first.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review PR 245 in owner/repo. Run read-only checks first. Summarize blockers before any GitHub action.

prompt_templates.title: Run Specialist Reviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill for PR 312. Coordinate code quality, security, performance, architecture, testing, and documentation reviews. Return prioritized findings.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Release Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review with integration and deployment focus.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a release PR. Include deployment impact, rollback readiness, feature flag needs, and final merge recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Review Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with explicit approval controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to conduct all four phases for PR 418. Do not change GitHub state until I approve the proposed final decision.

output_examples.input: Review a feature PR that adds email validation.
output_examples.output: Automated checks passed. Specialist review found three low-priority suggestions. Integration risk is low. Recommended decision is approve.

output_examples.input: Review a large API refactor before merge.
output_examples.output: The review found blocking security and performance issues, plus migration documentation gaps. Recommended decision is request changes with targeted follow-up review.
Security verification passed, tests are clean, and deployment impact is low. Recommended decision is approve after maintainer confirmation.

best_practices: Run read-only checks before any command that changes GitHub state.
Validate repository, pull request number, branch, and permissions before using command examples.
Store findings by phase so later reviewers can inspect earlier evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-merge or approve a pull request without explicit maintainer confirmation.
Do not treat sample thresholds as universal policy for every repository.
Do not run every specialist review for small changes when a narrower review is enough.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews pull requests across automated checks, code quality, security, performance, architecture, tests, documentation, and deployment impact.

faq.question: Does it require claude-flow?
faq.answer: The workflow examples use claude-flow commands. Teams can adapt the process to other agent orchestration tools.

faq.question: Can it approve or merge pull requests?
faq.answer: It includes example GitHub commands for approval and merge actions. Users should require explicit confirmation before running them.

faq.question: Is it suitable for small pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes, but teams should reduce the number of specialist reviews when the change is low risk.

faq.question: Does it replace human reviewers?
faq.answer: No. It organizes review work and evidence so human maintainers can make informed decisions.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: The examples assume GitHub CLI, claude-flow, language test tools, build tools, and jq where shell scripts are used.
